cases.reasoning: Both replies give explicit scoring formulas, confidence tiers, capacity by role, dependencies, a timeline, stakeholder rationales, risks and actions, and neither invents facts beyond flagged assumptions. A's arithmetic checks out (index values, 508 stores, roughly 3,560만 원 MRR at risk, the equal-weight sensitivity check). It also subtracts holidays and the designer's vacation from capacity, sets a POS cutover of 11/27 ahead of peak season, and makes 7 and 6 conditional with concrete triggers and dates. B's best contribution is the honest forecast that churn will land around 2.6-2.8% at the end of Q4 and the request for an executive decision to move the target. It also derives the 59% onboarding-registration rate correctly. However, B's churn effect estimates rest on assumed dunning recovery and a 1/3 effect for recommendations, and it drops the 알림톡 item outright. A is more rigorous and more actionable on sequencing and dependencies, though its opening questions and length add some weight.

The request has only seven feature names, so the right move is to ask focused questions and state assumptions rather than invent facts. A does this with explicit [ASSUMPTION] tags, a stated scoring method with a worked example (its arithmetic is correct), and confidence marked low everywhere. It says plainly that dependencies, deadlines and capacity could not be reflected, and it gives a tentative sequence and a cut list with re-entry conditions. B is honest and concise, with a reasonable draft and a useful list of what flips the ranking, but its scoring is only high/medium/low labels. It has no explicit confidence, no sequencing by week, and little on dependencies beyond a couple of remarks. A's numeric scores on invented inputs carry some false precision, but they are labeled, and A better meets the criteria on assumptions, confidence, dependencies and sequencing.

Both replies decline to reverse-engineer the weights and both offer an honest table plus a legitimate way to include the chatbot. A goes further on the criteria. It states weights before the results, gives a per-item confidence assessment, and demonstrates that the chatbot cannot win under any weighting because it is dominated by the reminder on every criterion. It also gives a capacity table showing only 2pw of slack, a stream schedule with ordering rationale and dependencies, and a cut list with re-entry conditions. It spells out the cost of the CEO's option: 4-5 week delays and the risk of cutting subscriptions. B is solid and concise, and its slide wording and the framing of the chatbot as a strategic bet are practical. But its plan is thinner, its sequencing is only a list, and it is internally inconsistent about the chatbot budget (10pw in the table versus a 2-3pw MVP). Its claim that the chatbot can't win under any weights is also vaguer.
